title: Mir Mannu's Death and the Opening of Mathura And Koel

blocks.text: The Mir Mannu episode reaches its climax as the trapped Sikh households lament that mothers and sisters had no one to share their grief while the minister's terror campaign seemed unstoppable. In the middle of that chaos, Mir Mannu's horse suddenly reared, threw him down, and his feet got entangled in the stirrup so that he was dragged to a painful death.

His fall is treated as divine reversal: the persecutor who meant to crush the Khalsa dies helplessly, and the machinery of the hunt breaks apart almost at once. Captives are released, the immediate panic lifts, and the narrative closes his episode by tying political justice to the downfall of a tyrant.

The same page then opens Episode About Mathura And Koel, widening the frame back to imperial politics after Panipat. Ahmad Shah Abdali now dominates the north, tribute flows from subordinate nawabs, and attention shifts toward Mathura and other Hindu centers that will define the next campaign.
